question: The maximum size of a land owned by a person is called___ (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019))
options: Land Revolution
Social Improvement
Land Policy for Farmers
Land Sealing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Land Sealing

Explanation:
Land Sealing refers to the maximum limit of land that can be owned by an individual or family. It is a key agrarian reform measure aimed at preventing unequal distribution of land and providing land to landless farmers. In India, various states have implemented land sealing acts. Under this policy, excess land is acquired by the government and distributed among the landless. Implementation of land sealing faces challenges such as manipulation of land records. The concept promotes social justice and economic equity in rural areas.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Main objective of Land Sealing → Ensure equitable distribution of land
☛ Under which program is Land Sealing implemented in India → Land Reforms Programme
☛ What happens to excess land under Land Sealing → Acquired by government and distributed to landless
☛ Land Sealing is related to which act → State Land Reforms Acts
☛ Why is Land Sealing opposed → Due to legal and administrative challenges by landowners

question: ​Where is the origin of Narmada River? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Trimbakeshwar Plateau near Nashik
Dandakaranya Plateau
Multai in Betul district
Amarkantak Plateau
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Amarkantak Plateau

Explanation:
The Narmada River originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh. It flows westward and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Narmada is one of the major west-flowing rivers of India and has a length of 1,312 km. It is considered the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Major projects like the Sardar Sarovar Dam and Indira Sagar Dam are built on this river. The Narmada has cultural significance since Vedic times and is also known as Reva.

question: Who is considered the father of Green Revolution in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: E Sreedharan
M. S. Swaminathan
Verghese Kurien
Chidambaram Subramaniam
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is M. S. Swaminathan

Explanation:
Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in India. In the 1960s, he developed high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, which dramatically increased food grain production and made India self-sufficient in food. His work transformed Indian agriculture and helped avert famine. Dr. Swaminathan was awarded the World Food Prize and the Padma Vibhushan for his contributions. He was born on August 7, 1925, in Tamil Nadu.

question: Amaravati School of Sculpture is built on the banks of which river? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Godavari River
Ganga River
Indus River
Krishna River
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Krishna River

Explanation:
The Amaravati School of Sculpture, also known as the Amaravati style of art, developed in South India. This sculptural style is primarily associated with the Amaravati Stupa located on the banks of the Krishna River in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh. It was a significant center of Buddhism. The Amaravati sculptures used white marble and depicted scenes from the life of Buddha. This style flourished during the Satavahana period (approximately 200 BCE to 200 CE). The characteristic features of Amaravati sculptures include intricate carvings and elongated, graceful figures. The school is known for its narrative panels and delicate detailing.

question: Which is the highest peak in South India? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: What are the high risk potential areas of earthquake called?   (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Environmental Zone
Plane Zone
Richter Zone
Seismic Zone
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seismic Zone

Explanation:
High risk potential areas of earthquakes are called Seismic Zones. These are regions with a higher probability of earthquake occurrence, classified according to seismic zoning maps. In India, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) divides the country into four seismic zones - Zone II, III, IV, and V, where Zone V has the highest risk. Other options like Richter Zone are incorrect because the Richter scale measures earthquake magnitude, not zones. Environmental Zone and Plane Zone are not related to earthquake risk.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What are seismic zones? → Areas with high earthquake probability.
☛ How many seismic zones are in India? → Four (II, III, IV, V)
☛ Which is the highest risk seismic zone in India? → Zone V
☛ Who prepares the seismic zoning map of India? → Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
☛ What does the Richter scale measure? → Earthquake magnitude

question: Which of the following is not included in the group of largest lakes?  (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)

Explanation:
'The Great Lakes' is a group of five large freshwater lakes located in North America. These include Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie, and Lake Ontario. These lakes are situated on the border between the United States and Canada and are among the largest freshwater reserves in the world. Lake Athabasca is a large lake located in Canada, but it is not part of the Great Lakes system. It spans across the provinces of Saskatchewan and Alberta. Therefore, among the given options, Lake Athabasca is the one not included in the Great Lakes, while the other three lakes are part of this group.

राजस्थान
गुजरात
तमिलनाडु
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पश्चिम बंगाल

Explanation:
दोराई पश्चिम बंगाल के बाँकुड़ा जिले में स्थित एक प्राचीन पुरातात्विक स्थल है। यह स्थल चोट नागपुर पठार के पूर्वी भाग में द्वारकेश्वर नदी के तट पर स्थित है। दोराई की खोज 2000 के दशक में हुई थी और यहाँ से प्रागैतिहासिक काल के पत्थर के औजार और मिट्टी के बर्तन मिले हैं। यह स्थल विशेष रूप से पूर्वपाषाण काल और मध्यपाषाण काल के साक्ष्य प्रदान करता है। दोराई की खुदाई से प्राप्त अवशेष बंगाल के प्राचीन मानव बस्तियों के अध्ययन में महत्वपूर्ण हैं। इस क्षेत्र में माइक्रोलिथ (सूक्ष्म पत्थर के औजार) भी प्रचुर मात्रा में मिले हैं।

question: Which type of soil covered most of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Alluvial Soil
Junky Rocky Soil
Red Soil
Black Soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial Soil

Explanation:
About 40% of India's land area is covered by Alluvial Soil. This soil is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers and is found in the northern plains, river valleys, and coastal regions. Alluvial soil is classified into Khadar (new) and Bhangar (old). It is highly fertile and ideal for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses. The soil is continuously replenished by the rivers originating from the Himalayas, making it one of the most productive soil types in India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Most widely spread soil in India → Alluvial Soil
☛ How many types of alluvial soil? → Two (Khadar and Bhangar)
☛ Where is Khadar soil found? → Flood plains of rivers
☛ Crops suitable for alluvial soil → Wheat, rice, sugarcane, pulses
☛ Main source of alluvial soil → Himalayan rivers
question_hi: भारत का अधिकांश भाग किस प्रकार की मिट्टी से ढका हुआ है? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: जलोढ़ मिट्टी
जंकी पथरीली मिट्टी
लाल मिट्टी
काली मिट्टी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जलोढ़ मिट्टी

Explanation:
भारत का लगभग 40% से अधिक भाग जलोढ़ मिट्टी से ढका हुआ है। यह मिट्टी नदियों द्वारा लाए गए अवसादों से बनी है और उत्तर भारत के मैदानों, नदी घाटियों और तटीय क्षेत्रों में पाई जाती है। जलोढ़ मिट्टी को खादर (नई) और बांगर (पुरानी) में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है। यह फसलों के लिए अत्यंत उपजाऊ होती है और गेहूं, चावल, गन्ना आदि की खेती के लिए आदर्श है। इसका निर्माण हिमालय से निकलने वाली नदियों द्वारा होता है, जो लगातार नई मिट्टी जमा करती हैं।

question: Which geographical features separate the the Andaman and Nicobar Islands? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Eight Point Bays
The narrow path of Duncan
Ten degree Channel
Coco Bay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ten Degree Channel

Explanation:
The Ten Degree Channel is the geographical feature that separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It is located at 10° North latitude and is approximately 150 km wide. The Andaman Islands lie to the north of this channel, while the Nicobar Islands are situated to the south. This channel connects the Bay of Bengal with the Andaman Sea and is important for maritime traffic. It is the southernmost island group of India and the region is rich in biodiversity.

question_hi: कौन सी भौगोलिक विशेषताएं अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह को अलग करती हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)

डंकन का संकरा रास्ता
दस डिग्री चैनल

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दस डिग्री चैनल

Explanation:
दस डिग्री चैनल अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह को अलग करने वाली भौगोलिक विशेषता है। यह चैनल 10° उत्तरी अक्षांश पर स्थित है और लगभग 150 किमी चौड़ा है। अंडमान द्वीप समूह इस चैनल के उत्तर में, जबकि निकोबार द्वीप समूह दक्षिण में स्थित है। यह चैनल बंगाल की खाड़ी और अंडमान सागर को जोड़ता है, और समुद्री यातायात के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है। यह भारत का दक्षिणीतम द्वीप समूह है और इस क्षेत्र में जैव विविधता समृद्ध है।

question: The Koleru lake is found in the triangle of ________. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Ganges and Mahanadi
Godavari and Krishna
Mahanadi and Godavari
Krishna and Kaveri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Godavari and Krishna

Explanation:
Kolleru Lake is a freshwater lake located in Andhra Pradesh, situated in the delta region between the Godavari and Krishna rivers. It lies in the triangular area formed by these two rivers. The lake is an important habitat for birds and is recognized as a Ramsar site. It spreads across the Guntur and Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh. The lake is also significant for fishing and agriculture.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है गोदावरी और कृष्णा

Explanation:
कोलेरू झील आंध्र प्रदेश में गोदावरी और कृष्णा नदियों के डेल्टा क्षेत्र के बीच स्थित एक मीठे पानी की झील है। यह दोनों नदियों के बीच के त्रिभुजाकार क्षेत्र में पाई जाती है, जिसे कोलेरू झील कहा जाता है। यह झील पक्षियों के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण आवास स्थल है और इसे रामसर स्थल के रूप में भी मान्यता प्राप्त है। यह आंध्र प्रदेश के गुंटूर और कृष्णा जिलों में फैली हुई है। यह झील मछली पकड़ने और कृषि के लिए भी महत्वपूर्ण है।
